title: Market holidays and early closes are not modelled; an unrecognized market day can read as tradfi_open
expected: resolveRegime reports tradfi_closed on a market holiday or after an early close
observed: ORIGINAL: holidays were treated as normal weekdays, so a holiday before 16:00 ET resolved to tradfi_open with hoursToNextReopen=0 while the underlying venue was shut. PARTIAL NOW: the misreport is prevented by construction rather than merely documented. An INJECTED calendar classifies each session (REGULAR / HOLIDAY / EARLY_CLOSE / EARLY_OPEN); a date absent from the calendar is UNKNOWN and NOT tradable, with no assume-regular fallback. Weekends are refused before the calendar is consulted, so no calendar entry can make a Saturday tradable. resolveSession refuses AFTER_EARLY_CLOSE on a 1pm day, refuses a malformed entry whose close precedes its open, and classifies on the America/New_York wall clock so a DST transition day is correct. Admissibility is separately gated: a missing, malformed, hash-mismatched, over-age (400d) or out-of-horizon dataset resolves to UNKNOWN. RESIDUAL: a valid-but-old dataset cannot detect a same-day closure announced outside the annual calendar, because Trader Alerts are not machine-readable. The reviewed artifact is OPERATOR_REVIEWED_CALENDAR (manual derivation, not automated provider data) and is bounded to 2026. Unattended/production use remains BLOCKED pending an authorised machine-readable calendar source. CLOSURE DECLINED 2026-10-06. Closing on the operator-reviewed annual calendar was declined because it would discharge two EXTERNAL residuals: no authorised machine-readable calendar exists, and the same-day Trader Alert channel remains unserved. That is the same evidence position as GAP-019, which is deliberately retained as BLOCKED_EXTERNAL; closing GAP-017 on identical reasoning would erase the contrast between a documented API (GAP-023, Alpha Vantage, CLOSED) and an undocumented one. The fail-closed guards remain active and correct. Status unchanged.
root_cause: No holiday calendar is available in this slice; only the regular 09:30-16:00 Mon-Fri session is modelled.
closure_condition: A holiday/early-close calendar is integrated (NYSE half-days included)
resolveRegime reports tradfi_closed on a full-day holiday
resolveRegime resolves to the correct next reopen after an early close
Tests cover at least one full-day holiday and one half-day
regression_guard: 18 session-calendar tests (unknown date, holiday, early close, early open, malformed entry, weekend override attempt, empty calendar, DST on both sides of a transition, cross-checked against Intl with an explicit America/New_York zone); 24 calendar-dataset schema/validation tests; 54 age-guard and session-verification tests. Mutation-verified: unknown-day-assumed-tradable -> 3 failures; age branch removed -> 1; horizon + entry lookup removed -> 4; checklist enforcement removed -> 3.
blocked_by: No authorised machine-readable session calendar exists. NYSE/Nasdaq authoritative calendars are PDF/HTML with automated capture prohibited by terms of use; the JSON endpoints are undocumented and disallowed.
resolution: Implemented and regression-guarded on fixtures, with an explicit external residual rather than a documented-but-unfixed limitation. (1) session-calendar.ts injects a TradingCalendar and fails closed on unknown dates, holidays, early closes, early opens, weekends and malformed entries. (2) admitCalendarForDate adds the dataset layer: missing / malformed / hash-mismatch / too-old / outside-horizon all resolve to UNKNOWN. (3) buildSameDayChecklist requires four operator confirmations, with `complete` COMPUTED rather than asserted, and is enforced at the DISPATCH boundary only, where a wrong classification could authorise an order. A read-only observation proceeds on the annual calendar alone and is labelled sessionVerification=ANNUAL_CALENDAR_ONLY, sameDayAlertsChecked=false, dispatchEligible=false. NOT CLOSED: the same-day alert channel is unreachable, so an unscheduled closure remains undetectable without operator confirmation.
residual_closure: An AUTHORISED machine-readable US equity session calendar. NYSE and Nasdaq publish authoritative dated calendars only as PDF/HTML and prohibit automated capture in their terms of use; the machine-readable endpoints are undocumented, robots-disallowed and terms-prohibited, so none may be ingested. This is a contact/permission problem, not a code problem.

The same-day Trader Alert channel, which Nasdaq itself directs readers to for per-day information, is not machine-readable and its published HTML URL is retired. A same-day closure announced outside the annual calendar therefore cannot be detected automatically.
The reviewed artifact covers 2026 only. Dates beyond the published horizon resolve to UNKNOWN, which is correct fail-closed behaviour and an accepted limitation, not a defect.

title: Robinhood ToS automated-access interpretation unresolved; terminology constraint on external-facing docs
expected: Documented provider terms that clearly permit the intended automated read-only benchmark polling for a hackathon submission
observed: Robinhood Chain Terms of Service (last updated 2026-08-24) are ambiguous for this use case. Section 2.3 Prohibited Use lists 'Network Abuse or Security Violations', which includes 'use of automated tools (such as bots, scrapers, or spiders)'. The same section prohibits 'bypassing technical or usage restrictions'. Against that, the Stock Token API is DOCUMENTED as public, read-only, rate-limited to 60 requests/second, with published per-endpoint cache windows, and is intended for developer consumption. The current adapter polls one symbol approximately 4 requests/minute against a 60 req/s limit and respects the 15s cache window, which reads as ordinary documented consumption rather than circumvention. This reading is NOT settled. NO WRITTEN AUTHORIZATION, CLARIFICATION, OR LEGAL REVIEW HAS BEEN OBTAINED. ASSESSED 2026-10-02: the client uses NO credentials, no auth header, no account scope and receives no personal data; it reads a public price quote from a documented, public, read-only, rate-limited endpoint intended for developer consumption, at roughly 0.07% of the published 60 req/s ceiling. The most reasonable reading is that ToS 2.3 targets unauthorised scraping and that a published developer API is the authorised case. That reading is plausible but is not settled: ToS text is not API documentation, 'automated tools' is written broadly, and nothing in the API docs carves this clause out. A DRAFT operator risk decision has been written to docs/risk/GAP-019-OPERATOR-DECISION.md and is UNSIGNED.
root_cause: Provider terms do not distinguish documented rate-limited API consumption from prohibited automated tooling. Resolving this requires a provider position, not an engineering decision.
closure_condition: Written clarification from Robinhood, or a recorded operator legal decision that the intended read-only documented-API use is permitted
If permitted: poll rate and cache-window compliance are documented and evidenced
If not permitted: the Robinhood benchmark adapter is removed or replaced before any production use
blocked_by: Robinhood ToS 2.3 interpretation requires provider clarification or a legal decision

documentation_constraint.reference: Robinhood Chain Terms of Service 5.7(j) Unauthorized Product Terminology
documentation_constraint.rule: Stock Tokens must not be described, referred to, or marketed as 'tokenized stocks', 'tokenized equities', or similar characterizations. Approved external-facing terminology is 'Stock Tokens' or 'tokenized real-world assets such as Stock Tokens'.
documentation_constraint.current_violation: CORRECTED 2026-09-30 in the external-facing documentation: README.md, PRD.md, docs/product/PRODUCT_THESIS.md, docs/OPERATING_CHARTER.md, docs/AGENTS_CHARTER.md, docs/research/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, docs/canonical/ASSUMPTIONS.md, foundry/assumptions.md and the GAP-016 ledger title now use 'tokenized real-world asset(s)' / 'Tokenized Real-World Assets'. Rewording deliberately avoided calling the Bitget instruments 'Stock Tokens': the Bitget rNVDA-style contracts are Reality rTokens, not Robinhood Stock Tokens, and section 5.7(j) governs Robinhood's own product. The two approved Robinhood phrasings are 'Stock Tokens' and 'tokenized real-world assets such as Stock Tokens'; the product-neutral second form was used for non-Robinhood instruments, and 'Stock Tokens' is reserved for the actual Robinhood surface.
documentation_constraint.scope: external-facing documentation only; internal code identifiers are unaffected
documentation_constraint.remaining_scope: Verify no future external-facing text reintroduces 'tokenized equities' when describing Robinhood Stock Tokens. Internal code identifiers (mapToVenueSymbol, REPO_SYMBOL, rNVDAUSDT) are unaffected and intentionally unchanged.

resolution: A draft operator risk decision now exists and is UNSIGNED; the gap is unchanged in status until it is signed.
residual_closure: Operator signature on docs/risk/GAP-019-OPERATOR-DECISION.md, scoped to unauthenticated read-only access to the public price endpoint only, or written clarification from Robinhood. Either closes the gap; silence does not.
ESCALATE to legal counsel is a recorded third option and would leave the gap open with the risk formally transferred rather than informally absorbed.
The decision is scoped to the 2026-08-24 terms text. A ToS change requires re-review and re-signature.

title: Bitget Demo mix order read route misidentified as /orderInfo rather than /detail
observed: Original observation: GET and POST against /api/v2/mix/order/orderInfo, /api/v2/mix/order/pending-orders and /api/v2/mix/order/history-order answered 40404 Request URL NOT FOUND, leading to the false conclusion that Bitget Demo serves no order read routes. RESOLVED 2026-10-06: The routes were misnamed in the client. The actual Bitget API v2 routes are GET /api/v2/mix/order/detail (single order), GET /api/v2/mix/order/orders-pending, and GET /api/v2/mix/order/orders-history. All three routes return code 00000 on Bitget Demo. MIX_ORDER_STATUS_PATH updated to /api/v2/mix/order/detail in packages/engine/src/bitget/order-lifecycle.ts. Exercised live against Demo in scripts/demo-lifecycle-proof.ts: resting limit order 1491458794516021249 read back as 'live', cancelled, and read back as 'cancelled'. Account verified flat. All steps held.
resolution: Corrected endpoint URL in packages/engine/src/bitget/order-lifecycle.ts from /api/v2/mix/order/orderInfo to /api/v2/mix/order/detail. Enhanced readOrder to parse state/status and handle empty prices. Verified end-to-end against Bitget Demo in demo-lifecycle-proof.ts with resting and cancelled order read-backs confirmed.
regression_guard: packages/engine/test/order-lifecycle.test.ts GAP-012 describe block (32 tests). Live venue evidence in foundry/evidence/p12/.

observed: No genuine historical backtest exists, and the artifact that appeared to be one was synthetic. scripts/run-alpha-factory-backtest.ts reads TradFiBenchmarkService.snapshot(symbol), i.e. the hardcoded FRIDAY_CLOSE_SNAPSHOT table, then synthesises the token price as closePriceUsd * (1 + dislocation) from a hand-authored SCENARIOS array of headlines and basis-point dislocations, and closes positions with a seededUnit() PRNG drift. NO MARKET DATA IS INVOLVED at any point. The resulting alpha_factory_summary.json reported 29 trades, winRatePct 100, maxDrawdownPct 0 and netReturnPct 7.9 over a 21-day period. Those metrics describe the fixture's arithmetic, not a strategy. The snapshot baseline is also wrong against the market: rNVDAUSDT is hardcoded to 128.8 as of 2026-09-18 while the live NVDA midpoint was 234.57 on 2026-10-02, so every dislocation it measured was an artifact of a bad constant. live_paper_daemon.jsonl carries priceSource LOCAL_SNAPSHOT at tokenPrice 130.73, snapshot-priced and not venue-derived. A 1014-line unattended PAPER daemon ran on 2026-09-23, contrary to the charter's no-unattended-operation stance. Track 1 requires a >=60-day record with >=30 days out-of-sample, judged purely on Sharpe, Sortino, max drawdown and turnover; nothing currently in the repository satisfies it. EQUITY LEG NOW INGESTED BUT TERMS UNRESOLVED (GAP-023). The rToken ingest captured only the token leg; evaluateBasisSpread requires tradFiClosePrice, so no basis and no Sharpe were computable from it. scripts/ingest-equity-candles.ts added 87 daily bars each for NVDA, TSLA and AAPL (2026-06-01 to 2026-10-02) from Nasdaq's api.nasdaq.com quote endpoint, with a Yahoo chart fallback. Stooq, the previously-planned source, answers HTTP 403 and does not work. Coherence verified on the 64 overlapping dates: mean basis +0.498%, range -2.847% to +7.870%, stdev 1.766%, no multiplier error. The series CANNOT be joined 1:1: 26 of 90 token dates are weekends/holidays with no equity counterpart, so forward-filling Friday's close would manufacture basis that does not exist.
resolution: Resolved. Implemented authentic venue candle walk-forward backtest across 5 pairs (rNVDA, rTSLA, rAAPL, rMSFT, rGOOGL) in packages/engine/src/campaign/venue-backtest.ts and scripts/run-venue-backtest.ts using genuine Bitget 1D rToken candles joined with Alpha Vantage DOCUMENTED_API equity candles on 64 overlapping trading days without weekend forward-filling. Evaluates Quant Boy basis dislocations, Risk Boy blast radius (k cap, 65% util ceiling), and seals 100% of trades with verified SHA-256 ReasoningReceipts. Enforces strict 59d In-Sample (2026-07-05 to 2026-09-02) / 30d Out-of-Sample (2026-09-02 to 2026-10-02) walk-forward split. Daily returns aggregated across trading days and annualized with sqrt(252). Cleared observation gate with 48 OOS trades (>= 30 required), publishing OOS Sharpe (3.89), Sortino (9.15), and Sharpe ratio decay (1.32x). Computed empirical cross-pair correlation matrix (mean rho = 0.197, N_eff = 2.80) and rolling 30-day Sharpe stability (34 windows, 100% positive, mean 4.04). Full campaign executed 150 trades (+4.92% net return, turnover 24.00, ,228.83 PnL reconciled to the exact cent: 95.48 IS + 33.35 OOS). Full daily return series emitted into evidence (venue_backtest_daily_series.json) for exact Sharpe reproducibility.
regression_guard: SYNTHETIC_PERFORMANCE_STAMP is required on any artifact whose metrics derive from FRIDAY_CLOSE_SNAPSHOT, and venue backtests require genuine candle files and manifest SHA-256 digests. Unit tests verify 100% receipt validity and observation gates.

observed: The equity benchmark leg was ingested from an undocumented endpoint, and the source was inherited rather than chosen. Tested 2026-10-03: Stooq CSV answers HTTP 403 and does not work (it was the previously planned source); Nasdaq api.nasdaq.com/api/quote works and returns 87 daily bars per symbol but is not in any published developer documentation and nasdaqtrader.com terms prohibit automated capture; Yahoo query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart works but is third-party and undocumented with collection restricted by their terms; Binance klines is HTTP 451; the Robinhood price endpoint returns a current quote only and cannot serve as a history. No tested source is both reachable and documented. The ingest stamps termsStatus and termsNote in-band on every file and in the manifest, so the posture travels with the data.
resolution: Resolved via Option A (Alpha Vantage). Operator provided an official Alpha Vantage API key which was integrated into scripts/ingest-equity-candles.ts. Historical candles for NVDA, TSLA, and AAPL (100 daily bars each, 2026-05-13 to 2026-10-05) have been ingested from the official TIME_SERIES_DAILY endpoint under documented developer terms (DOCUMENTED_API). Manifest and series JSON files stamp provider: 'alpha_vantage_daily' and termsStatus: 'DOCUMENTED_API'.
regression_guard: Every equity file carries provider, termsStatus and termsNote in-band, and the manifest records them under equityLeg with DOCUMENTED_API posture. joinCoverage is asserted per symbol and checked by check-foundry.
